chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

'The divorce for the waiting period ('idda) is that the man divorces his wife at every period of purity (tuhr), sending a message to her: "Observe your waiting period, for so-and-so has divorced you."' He said: 'And he has the greater right to revoke it as long as her waiting period has not expired.'

key_terms.الرَّجْعَة: Revocation (raj'a): the husband's right to take back his wife during the waiting period without a new marriage contract
key_terms.الطَّلَاق لِلْعِدَّة: Divorce for the waiting period (talaq al-'idda): a specific form of revocable divorce that conforms to the procedural requirements of Islamic law
key_terms.الطُّهْر: Period of purity (tuhr): the interval between menstrual cycles during which a revocable divorce must be pronounced
key_terms.العِدَّة: Waiting period ('idda): the mandatory period a divorced woman must observe before she may remarry

ai.seo_question: What is the proper procedure for pronouncing a revocable divorce (talaq al-'idda) according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) defines the proper form of a revocable divorce (talaq al-'idda): the husband must pronounce the divorce during a period of purity (tuhr), then notify his wife that her waiting period ('idda) has begun. The Imam further clarifies that the husband retains the right of revocation (raj'a) throughout the entire waiting period, emphasizing both the procedural requirement and the husband's ongoing right to reconciliation. This hadith reflects the Shia jurisprudential framework for proper divorce procedure, distinguishing the revocable divorce from other forms and ensuring the wife is informed of her legal status.
word_analysis: to revoke (her divorce)/to take her back

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The divorce for the waiting period is that the man divorces his wife during every purity, sending a message to her that, ‘Begin her waiting period, for so and so has divorced you’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And he is in control with reverting back to her for as long as she has not fulfilled her waiting period’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn abu Najran from ‘Asem ibn Hamid from Muhammad ibn Qays who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Divorce with waiting period is that by which a man divorces his wife whenever she is clean of Hayd (menses) and sends her a message to commence her waiting period because so and so has divorced her.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He has the authority to go back to her as long as waiting period is not complete.’”
